source.source: HYG v4.4 (Hipparcos-Yale-Gliese Database, D. Nash / astronexus)
source.epoch: ICRS/J2000 equinox; source astrometry primarily Hipparcos-2007 reduction, epoch J1991.25
source.sentinelDistDoc: dist == 100000.0 marks an unmeasurable/negative Hipparcos parallax; rows with it are dropped, not shipped.
source.hipSentinelDoc: hip == 0 means the row has no Hipparcos catalogue number.

galacticFrame.source: Hipparcos Catalogue vol. 1 §1.5.3 (ESA SP-1200, 1997); J2000 galactic frame constants shared by astropy and SOFA

panorama.title: The Milky Way panorama
panorama.longitudeConvention: l = 0 at the column centre, increasing leftward (sky seen from inside)
panorama.latitudeConvention: b = +90 at row 0, -90 at the last row

catalogRegistration.role: retained source record only; the photograph is registered astrometrically and owns visible stars

pointSourcePresentation.positionSource: licensed ESO photographic local maxima; no Google catalogue bytes
pointSourcePresentation.qualification: native fixed-size catalogue behavior collapsed into the prepared cubemap; point positions and colors remain ESO-derived

sky.qualification: source-photographed full sky sampled in ICRF through the J2000 galactic frame and the anchor-registered panorama; the scene registration carries the Gaspra pole and epoch; Solar System objects in the mosaic are capture artefacts; no Sun is baked into the cubemap
sky.sceneRegistrationChain: galactic -> ICRF (J2000 constants) -> body-fixed (IAU pole and prime meridian at the epoch) -> ecliptic presentation frame

analyticRadialFit.qualification: Least-squares fit to annular red-channel means from the bound native 128 by 128 Sun texture; fitted values only, no source pixels.

distanceScaling.qualification: The opaque photospheric core is projected from the IAU nominal solar radius and the object catalog's mean heliocentric distance. The retained glow profile remains a visual presentation; the distance is not epoch-specific.

provenance.source: Pinned JPL Horizons heliocentric elements and the source mission body-fixed rotation model
provenance.qualification: Computed Gaspra Sun direction at 2026-09-03T00:00:00 TT, expressed in the ecliptic presentation frame (north up, Sun left at zero yaw) and in view space at the default camera pose.

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.description: Galileo’s highest-resolution pair, 107318313 and 107318326, mapped onto the Thomas shape. The source is high-pass filtered and retains photographed illumination; it is not calibrated albedo or natural color. Best original detail is approximately 55 m/pixel and varies greatly. The gray grid marks poor or missing coverage. Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting.
controls.summary: Photographed shadows and seams remain after mapping the images onto the shape. The gray grid marks poor or missing data.
controls.title: SSI monochrome mosaic

controls.label: SSI reflectance
controls.description: These Galileo close-ups cover opposite ends of Gaspra. They were taken through a clear filter and show the sunlight and shadows from the flyby. The grid marks areas without usable photographs.
controls.summary: These Galileo close-ups cover opposite ends of Gaspra. They were taken through a clear filter and show the sunlight and shadows from the flyby. The grid marks areas without usable photographs.
controls.title: Calibrated Galileo photographs

controls.label: Elevation
controls.description: Color shows the published shape radius minus a 6.1 km reference sphere, including Gaspra’s broad irregular shape. This is shape-derived height, not gravitational elevation or a photographic observation. Shape constraints vary with the flyby coverage; unseen regions are less certain. Brightness adds cartographic relief; Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting.
controls.summary: Height relative to a 6.1 km sphere, including Gaspra's broad shape. The unseen side is less certain.
controls.title: Shape-derived radial height
